intro: This question helps us find the best place for you to begin.

widget.instructions: The board shows the box's weight and the normal force. Add other forces with Precise controls, drag their tips, then press Play to see how the moving box would respond.

stem: A {{m}} kg box slides to the right at {{v0}} m/s across a rough floor. Your push has already ended.
Which forces act on the box now?

options.text: Its weight (from the Earth), the normal force (from the floor) and friction from the floor, pointing left
Its weight, the normal force, friction pointing left, and the force of your push pointing right
Its weight, the normal force and a forward “force of motion” that keeps it going

args.label: with a forward force of motion

options.text: Only its weight and the normal force: nothing acts along the floor

answerText: Weight, the normal force and friction pointing left

hints.text: A force needs an agent: something touching the box, or the Earth's gravity. What is touching the box now?
Add a Push to the right, press Play, and watch the speed. Does a sliding box on a rough floor really speed up?
The box is slowing down. Slowing down needs a net force pointing backwards.

extra-force-of-motion.text: Once your hand leaves the box, your push stops acting. Nothing pushes the box forward: it keeps moving because of inertia. The dashed box shows what your choice predicts; a real box slows down.

missing-friction.text: Without friction, nothing would slow the box: the dashed box keeps sliding at a constant speed. The rough floor exerts friction against the motion.

generic.text: List only forces with an agent touching the box now, plus gravity. Then ask whether those forces explain the box slowing down.

workedSolution.text: Agents acting on the box now: the Earth (gravity) and the floor (contact). Your hand is no longer touching it.
The floor pushes up (normal force) and rubs against the motion (friction, pointing left).
Net force: friction of {{f}} N to the left, so the box decelerates at {{f/m}} m/s² and slows down. Press Play to watch.

extra-force-of-motion.front: A box slides after you stop pushing. Is your push still a force on it?
extra-force-of-motion.back: No. Every force needs an agent in contact (or a field). The box keeps moving because of inertia, and friction slows it.

missing-friction.front: What slows a box sliding across a rough floor?
missing-friction.back: Kinetic friction from the floor, pointing opposite the motion.

generic.front: How do you decide which forces act on a body?
generic.back: Find each agent: things in contact with it, plus gravity. No agent, no force.

accessibility.altText: A box on a floor moving right at {{v0}} m/s, with its weight drawn down and the normal force drawn up.
